rule: When inspecting mock call arguments with `call_args`, first assert the mock was called exactly once with `assert_called_once()` or `assert call_count == 1`.
trigger: diff adds `mock_*.call_args` access without a preceding `assert_called_once()` or `call_count` check
rationale: Without an explicit call-count assertion, a test silently passes even when the mocked constructor/function is never called or called multiple times, hiding real regressions.

rule: Do not place type-stub packages (e.g. `types-*`) in provider runtime `dependencies`; put them in the dev/type-check dependency group only.
trigger: diff adds a `types-*` package to the `[project] dependencies` list in a provider `pyproject.toml`
rationale: Type stubs are only useful at type-check time; shipping them in runtime dependencies forces every `pip install` of the provider to pull down stubs users never need.

evidence.excerpt: Type stubs should not be installed at runtime — only useful at type-check time

rule: Behaviour changes to public provider hook methods (e.g. return-value shape, filtering of entries) must be documented in the provider's `docs/changelog.rst` under the next release version.
trigger: diff alters the return value or filtering logic of an existing public provider hook method without adding an entry to `docs/changelog.rst`
rationale: Users relying on the old behaviour (e.g. iterating `list_directory` results including `.`/`..`) will see silent breakage; a changelog entry gives them a chance to adapt.

evidence.excerpt: Add entry to `providers/sftp/docs/changelog.rst` explaining the behaviour change

rule: Do not silently change the API contract of an existing async hook method; if new behaviour (e.g. recursive walk, full-path return) is desired, add an explicit flag parameter or a separate method.
trigger: diff modifies an existing async hook method so that it returns a different structure or traverses more than the previous implementation, without a new parameter to opt in
rationale: The async and sync variants of a hook method are expected to share the same API contract; silently changing one breaks callers and breaks parity with the sync counterpart.

evidence.excerpt: Consider adding an explicit `recursive` flag or a separate method

rule: Process-wide singleton pools must not implement `__aenter__`/`__aexit__` context-manager protocol unless they own a truly scoped lifecycle; use an explicit lifecycle hook instead.
trigger: diff adds `__aenter__` / `__aexit__` to a class that stores itself in a module-level `_instances` dict (singleton pattern)
rationale: Mixing global-singleton state with deceptive local `async with` syntax means one caller's exit can close the pool for all concurrent callers in the same process.

evidence.excerpt: Global state with deceptively local syntax — drop __aenter__/__aexit__ or drop singleton

rule: When a provider notifier adds version-gated behaviour via `AIRFLOW_V_x_y_PLUS`, evaluate whether the guard belongs in `BaseNotifier` rather than duplicated in every concrete notifier.
trigger: diff adds `if AIRFLOW_V_x_y_PLUS:` version guard inside a concrete `Notifier.__init__` or `notify()` method
rationale: Centralising version guards in `BaseNotifier` avoids copy-paste across all notification providers and keeps the compatibility surface in one place.

evidence.excerpt: Should we add a check in the BaseNotifier instead?

rule: Before calling `response.raise_for_status()` against a provider API, log the error response body so that upstream error messages are preserved for debugging.
trigger: diff adds `response.raise_for_status()` without a preceding log statement that captures the response body on 4xx/5xx
rationale: Provider APIs (e.g. Snowflake) return structured error messages; raising immediately discards that context, making failures harder to diagnose.

evidence.excerpt: Log the error with the response before raising

rule: Hard-coded timeouts for long-running provider API calls (e.g. agent or ML model requests) must be exposed as a configurable operator/hook parameter rather than a module-level constant.
trigger: diff introduces a module-level `*_TIMEOUT` constant that gates an HTTP request to a long-running provider API (ML/agent/query workloads) without a corresponding constructor parameter
rationale: Snowflake Cortex Agents can legitimately run for up to 15 minutes; a fixed 60-second default silently aborts valid workloads for users with longer-running jobs.

evidence.excerpt: Make this a parameter that the user can configure

rule: Push deferrable-operator query/job identifiers to XCom immediately after they are obtained, before entering the poll loop, so they survive task failure.
trigger: diff moves an `xcom_push` call for query/job IDs to after a polling loop in a deferrable operator's `execute` or equivalent method
rationale: If a polled statement errors mid-loop the handles are lost; pushing IDs before polling lets users look up failed statements in the provider's console.

evidence.excerpt: Pushing query_ids after the loop — a failure now loses them

rule: Use `try/except ImportError` instead of `if AIRFLOW_V_x_y_PLUS` guards when importing symbols that moved between `airflow.sdk` and `airflow.providers` or `airflow.sensors`.
trigger: diff adds `if AIRFLOW_V_x_y_PLUS: from airflow.sdk... else: from airflow.sensors...` or similar SDK/provider import split
rationale: `AIRFLOW_V_x_y_PLUS` checks core version semantics which is not correct for SDK/provider compatibility boundaries; `try/except ImportError` is more robust and avoids introducing new version-guarded import branches.

evidence.excerpt: Better to have try/except — more robust, not introduce new `AIRFLOW_V_x_y_PLUS` checks

rule: Use `@cached_property` for expensive connection initialisation in provider hooks rather than eagerly constructing clients in `__init__`.
trigger: diff constructs a provider client (e.g. `zenpy_client`, `_hook`, API sessions) in `Hook.__init__` instead of a `@cached_property`
rationale: Lazy initialisation via `@cached_property` avoids network calls at import/instantiation time and aligns with the Airflow hook convention of deferring connection until first use.

rule: Document all supported connection extra keys and their precedence order in the hook's `_init_conn` (or equivalent) docstring.
trigger: diff adds multiple `extra.get(...)` branches to a hook's connection-init method without a docstring describing the supported keys and precedence
rationale: Users configure Airflow connections through the UI; without documentation of accepted extra fields and their priority, the authentication options are effectively undiscoverable.

evidence.excerpt: Document supported extra keys and precedence in the `_init_conn` docstring

rule: Provider logo assets must live under the `providers/` directory tree, not under a parallel top-level `registry/` folder.
trigger: diff adds image or logo files under `registry/` rather than under `providers/<name>/`
rationale: Keeping logos co-located with their provider avoids a parallel inventory and keeps provider assets self-contained.

evidence.excerpt: Move logos to providers folder; avoid another parallel inventory

rule: When checking whether a sentinel value is `NOTSET`, use the `is_arg_set()` helper from `airflow.serialization.definitions.notset` rather than inline `is NOTSET` comparisons, and annotate the parameter with `ArgNotSet` in its type signature.
trigger: diff adds `if value is NOTSET` / `if param is NOTSET` checks without using `is_arg_set()` and without `ArgNotSet` in the parameter type annotation
rationale: Using `is_arg_set()` is the idiomatic Airflow pattern for `NOTSET` sentinel checks and also lets mypy narrow the type correctly without extra `# type: ignore` comments.

evidence.excerpt: `is_arg_set` helper might be more appropriate to distinguish the `NOTSET`

rule: Shared type-dispatch logic for `str | datetime | None` parameters should be extracted into a common utility rather than repeated across multiple methods or operators.
trigger: diff duplicates `isinstance(value, (str, datetime.datetime))` dispatch blocks for the same logical parameter in more than one method
rationale: Parameters like `logical_date` and `run_after` follow the same `None | datetime | str` coercion pattern; a shared util prevents divergence between the two paths.

evidence.excerpt: Worthwhile to have common utils to handle the type across `None | datetime | str`

rule: When generating Alembic migration revision messages from shell scripts, pass the message as a single quoted string, not via `"${@}"`, to avoid multi-word arguments being split into multiple Alembic args.
trigger: diff passes `"${@}"` as the `-m` argument to `alembic revision --autogenerate`
rationale: Shell word-splitting on `${@}` passes extra tokens as unexpected Alembic positional arguments when the script is invoked with a multi-word message.

evidence.excerpt: `-m "${@}"` splits into multiple args; Alembic treats extra tokens as unexpected arguments
